response.sql: WITH p AS (SELECT P.ID, P.SEX, AVG(L.ALB) AS alb, AVG(L.UN * 1.0 / NULLIF(L.`T-BIL`, 0)) AS ratio FROM Laboratory L JOIN Patient P ON P.ID = L.ID GROUP BY P.ID, P.SEX), s AS (SELECT SEX, AVG(alb) AS avg_alb, AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio FROM p GROUP BY SEX), m AS (SELECT AVG(avg_alb) AS mean_alb FROM s) SELECT s.SEX, s.avg_alb, s.avg_ratio, s.avg_alb - m.mean_alb AS alb_above_mean FROM s CROSS JOIN m WHERE s.avg_alb > m.mean_alb

assumptions.assumption: A ratio can't be computed when T-BIL is 0 or NULL, or UN is NULL; those test rows are ignored in the ratio average. T-BIL = 0 is treated as not computable.
The mean of the sex-level ALB averages is the unweighted average over the sex groups present in the data. A NULL or empty SEX value, if present, counts as its own group.
